thread.title: Morning Movers: Dow Rebounds Even as Pfizer, Procter Tumble

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Morning Movers: Dow Rebounds Even as Pfizer, Procter Tumble
text:
By Teresa Rivas July 31, 2018 9:21 a.m. ET Goodbye July. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is rising today, as investors hope that Apple (AAPL) earnings will help to get tech stocks back on track . Earnings have been relatively strong this season, and tomorrow we'll hear from the Federal Reserve . In today's Morning Movers , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...review how earnings season has shaken out so far;
•...debate what might be ahead for August;
•....and note Archer Daniels Midland 's (ADM) 5% jump.
Dog Days Ahead?
Stocks appear ready to open higher after slumping to start the week, helped by the Bank of Japan's decision to hold interest rates steady and anticipation of more big earnings.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is rising 0.1% in early trading, while the S&P 500 is up 0.3% and the Nasdaq Composite is 0.4% higher.
The market has held up relatively well despite tech's selloff, as there's more than one way to get to new highs. Faang stocks— Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL)—officially closed in correction territory yesterday, a rare second correction in a single year for the quintet. Apple reports after the bell today, which may provide some direction for the divided Faang group.
Earnings in general have been strong this quarter, however, with 83% of companies beating expectations and earnings per share up 23% year over year. "This may be the peak for US EPS growth with many companies guiding down for the rest of the year, but we believe the US will continue to outpace the rest of the developed world, supported by strong domestic growth, a capex recovery and resilient margins," writes HSBC's Ben Laidler.
Certainly, some investors have been worried that the breadth of gains has narrowed, with the top-10 contributors generating 62% of the S&P 500's year-to-date returns, writes Goldman Sachs' David Kostin. While breadth has signaled below-average prospect returns in the past, he notes that today it "remains above levels that have historically been warning signs. Fundamentally, earnings strength remains healthy and broad-based; the median S&P 500 stock has higher 2019 consensus EPS growth than the broad index (10% vs. 9%)."
Today is also the last day of the month for July, and if the market can close in the black, it will be the 18th month of gains out of the last 21. So what could investors expect for August?
CFRA' Sam Stovall notes that since World War II, the S&P 500 has gained about 1%, on average, in July of a midterm-election years, but has dropped in August, which ranks as one of the three worst months. Some of the deepest pain was 20 years ago, when the S&P 500 fell 14.6% in August 1998. LPL Research Senior Market Strategist Ryan Detrick is even less sanguine about what may lie ahead, as he notes that since 1980, "there is no month with a worse average return when it is lower than August."
That said, Detrick still thinks that by year end, the market will be up 10%. So even if August brings summer storms, it seems they won't turn into a hurricane.
Morning Movers
Earnings & News
AK Steel (AKS) is down 9.7% to $4.84 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The steel firm earned 22 cents a share on revenue of $1.75 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 21 cents on revenue of $1.75 billion.
Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is up 5.8% to $501.0 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The agricultural products maker earned $1.02 a share on revenue of $17.07 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 77 cents on revenue of $15.48 billion.
Illustration: DOMINICK REUTER/AFP/Getty Images KLA-Tencor (KLAC) is up 3.6% to $110.11 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The chip equipment maker earned $2.22 a share on revenue of $1.07 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.12 on revenue of $1.05 billion.
Pfizer (PFE) is down 1.5% to $38.02 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The drugmaker earned 81 cents a share on revenue of $13.47 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 74 cents on revenue of $13.3 billion. For the full year, it expects EPS of $2.95 to $3.05, on revenue of $53 billion to $55 billion. Consensus calls for earnings of $2.95 on revenue of $54.25 billion.
Procter & Gamble (PG) is down 1.5% to $79 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The personal care products maker earned 94 cents a share on revenue of $16.5 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 90 cents on revenue of $16.52 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $4.35 to $4.56, on revenue of $66.8 billion to $67.5 billion. Consensus calls for earnings of $4.39 on revenue of $67.74 billion.
Transocean (RIG) is up 1.4% to $13.57 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The oil-field services operator lost 4 cents a share, on revenue of $790 million. Analysts were looking for an 18 cent loss on revenue of $768.7 million.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images Upgrades & Downgrades
Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) is up 1.6% to $45.50 after Raymond James upgraded it to Outperform.
Caterpillar (CAT) is down 0.6% to $138.88 after Barclays downgraded it to Equal Weight.
Lear (LEA) is up 1.6% to $180.49 after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to Overweight.
Signet Jewelers (SIG) is down 1.4% to $60.75 after Instinet downgraded it to Neutral.
Tupperware (TUP) is down 0.9% to $36.73 after Argus downgraded it to Sell.
Twitter (TWTR) is up 1.2% to $31.37 after Instinet upgraded it to Neutral.
